stem:
Pranav studies the diagram of triangles $PQR$ and $XYZ$. Matching tick marks show $PQ=XY$, $QR=YZ$, and $RP=ZX$.

Which claim correctly decides congruence from those side lengths?

options.text: The triangles are congruent: three corresponding equal side lengths are enough.
Equal side lengths appear only after congruence is already known, so sides cannot settle it.
An included matching angle between two of those sides is also required before congruence can be decided.
Same shape alone is enough even when the three side lengths do not match.

teacher.key_rationale: SSS: three corresponding equal sides guarantee congruence. Saying sides follow only after congruence reverses the test; requiring an included angle conflates SAS; same shape without matching sides substitutes a weaker label.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as two triangles PQR and XYZ with SSS tick marks on corresponding sides.
